Algorithm 1 Diversity Filter   
Require: A set of pairs $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{in}} = \{(x_1,y_1),\dots ,(x_{|P|},y_{|P|})\}$ generated using the same prefix $c$ Ensure:Filtered set of pairs $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}$ $E\gets \emptyset$ for $i,j\in [1,|P|],i\neq j$ do $\triangleright$ search for duplicate pairs if $P_{NLI}(x_i\Rightarrow x_j) > \tau_{entail}$ then $E\gets E\cup \{(x_i,y_i),(x_j,y_j)\}$ else if $P_{NLI}(y_i\Rightarrow y_j) > \tau_{entail}$ then $E\gets E\cup \{(x_i,y_i),(x_j,y_j)\}$ end if   
end for $G\gets (\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{in}},E)$ define a graph where nodes are pairs and edges connect duplicate pairs $S\gets$ Connected-Components(G) $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}\gets \emptyset$ for $C\in S$ do $\triangleright$ find the max-entailing pair in each connected component $p_{\mathrm{out}} = \operatorname {argmax}_{(x,y)\in C}P_{NLI}(x\Leftrightarrow y)$ $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}\gets \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}\cup \{p_{\mathrm{out}}\}$ end for

As noted in Section 3.5, we start off using GPT2-XL and BioGPT-large as teacher LM - all with 1.5B parameters - generating paraphrases in general and biomedical domain respectively. To sample contextual constraints from these LMs, we use Nucleus Sampling with top_p = 0.9 and temp = 1.0. Additionally, we find that for general domain, generating new-style sentences by prompting GPT2 with a simple prefix (e.g., New York (CNN) -) leads to less noisy and more diverse context. For BioGPT, we free-form generate without any prefix given. Throughout the distillation process, we used 4 Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs.

Algorithm 1 Diversity Filter   
Require: A set of pairs $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{in}} = \{(x_1,y_1),\dots ,(x_{|P|},y_{|P|})\}$ generated using the same prefix $c$ Ensure:Filtered set of pairs $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}$ $E\gets \emptyset$ for $i,j\in [1,|P|],i\neq j$ do $\triangleright$ search for duplicate pairs if $P_{NLI}(x_i\Rightarrow x_j) > \tau_{entail}$ then $E\gets E\cup \{(x_i,y_i),(x_j,y_j)\}$ else if $P_{NLI}(y_i\Rightarrow y_j) > \tau_{entail}$ then $E\gets E\cup \{(x_i,y_i),(x_j,y_j)\}$ end if   
end for $G\gets (\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{in}},E)$ define a graph where nodes are pairs and edges connect duplicate pairs $S\gets$ Connected-Components(G) $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}\gets \emptyset$ for $C\in S$ do $\triangleright$ find the max-entailing pair in each connected component $p_{\mathrm{out}} = \operatorname {argmax}_{(x,y)\in C}P_{NLI}(x\Leftrightarrow y)$ $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}\gets \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{out}}\cup \{p_{\mathrm{out}}\}$ end for
